models_evaluated: four LLMs (not named in the text)

links.outcome: Causal effect of proxy attributes on LLM clinical-ranking decisions versus warranted reliance
links.effect: Under neutral labels every model relies on proxies with no information. Informative proxies draw over-reliance, warranted and under-reliance. Reliance severely undertracks the evidence.
links.quote: Under neutral labels every model relies on proxies with no information.

links.outcome: Whether LLMs rely on proxy features in line with their predictive evidence
links.effect: Reliance on proxies is uncalibrated to predictive evidence; social-label suppression is fragile, since in-context examples raise reliance above zero in every model. Accuracy-based evaluation detects none of this.

unlisted_practices: Comparing measured proxy reliance against the exactly computed evidence-warranted reference, so one audit signal separates over-reliance, warranted reliance and under-reliance
Using social versus neutral field names to suppress proxy reliance

screen.reason: Empirical audit assessing fairness/proxy reliance of LLMs in a clinical-ranking/triage task, but it evaluates model behavior rather than testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
